messages:
Sam: Heads-up — hitting a weird mismatch between service-bound roles and route-level quotas in the console. Tenant X shows 'no access' for the /infer route even though the API returns 200 for some calls. Anyone run into this?
Priya: saw this yesterday on tenant-beta. Console UI rendered 'no access' but calls to /v1/infer with token succeeded for short payloads. feels like a rendering vs auth check split. :thinking_face:
Leo: can you paste the failing flow + the console/API responses? helps debug race vs data model mismatch.
Sam: sure, pasted request/response we saw:
```
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" https://api.redwood.example/v1/infer -d '{"model":"rwd-alpha","input":"hi"}'
# -> 200 {"id":"r_123","output":"hello"}
```
Console network trace when previewing permissions showed: `GET /admin/tenants/X/effective-permissions` -> 200 but payload has `{"/infer": {"allowed": false, "reason":"route-override-denies"}}`
Priya: looks like the console is only reading aggregated tenant entitlements and not considering route-level quota exceptions that the runtime uses at request-time.
Irene: yep — this is because the "effective-permissions" aggregator we built flattens by role set and stops at tenant-level deny. Runtime routing policies evaluate route-scoped overrides and quota buckets later in the request path, so there is a semantic mismatch.
Marta: proposal: twofold change — 1) make console preview surface both the computed decision and the decision sources (role, route-override, quota) so users can see why something is blocked; 2) extend admin API to return per-resource "sources" array so UI doesn't have to re-derive.
Priya: +1. Example API contract suggestion:
```
GET /v1/admin/tenants/:id/effective-permissions
200 [
  {"resource":"/infer","action":"invoke","allowed":false,
   "sources":["role:reader","route-override:deny","quota:exceeded:window=1m"]
  }
]
```
Sam: that payload would exactly fix the UX. also we'd show a small badge "denied by route override" with tooltip explaining next steps.
Leo: perf caveat — computing the full sources for every permission on every console load could be expensive for large tenants with many routes. We should cache snapshots and invalidate only on relevant changes (role binding change, route policy edit, quota policy edit). Prefer event-driven invalidation hooks over naive TTL.
Irene: agreed. pattern: build per-tenant snapshot doc in datastore (materialized), update via change events from identity/route services. Keep a short fallback TTL for safety.
Marta: telemetry: add a permission-preview event `permissions_preview.view` with fields {tenant_id, viewer_id, compute_time_ms, snapshot_age_ms, discrepancy_count}. That will help us monitor user-visible mismatches and perf regressions.
Priya: for rollout: feature-flag `ep_sources_v1` targeting internal + early customers. Start with read-only console preview and API behind flag. Gradual enablement and collect telemetry. If snapshot compute spikes, fallback to previous aggregator.
deploy-bot: deploy-bot: canary rollout of permissions-snapshotter v3 started (deploy id infra-2467) :rocket:
Sam: I'll open the API PR with the shape above and a migration note. @Leo can you add the invalidation hooks? @Priya can you mock UI chips and the tooltip microcopy?
Priya: will mock. sending sketches to #design later today. :thumbsup:
Leo: yep, I'll add hooks to identity-service and route-service and a small job to rebuild snapshots for affected tenant on change. Will also add a perf budget test.
Marta: adding rollout checklist items: feature-flag gating, canary to internal orgs, telemetry on compute_time + errors, ops runbook to revert snapshotter, and docs for admins about "why access differs".
Sam: awesome. Sync tomorrow 10am to align API + cache contract. Thanks everyone.
thread_summary: Short thread discussing mismatch between console effective-permissions and runtime route-level evaluation. Proposed API change to include 'sources' per permission, caching/invalidation strategy, telemetry events, and a feature-flagged gradual rollout with canary deploys.
